newsitem.title: USA: ADT set to launch car tracking service.
newsitem.headline: ADT set to launch car tracking service.

text.p: ADT Ltd., the largest electronic security firm n North America and Britain, is breaking into the vehicle protection business.
The Boca Raton, Fla-based company next month will begin selling CARCOP, an electronic vehicle tracking system that is designed to help motorists with everything from lost keys to carjackings.
"We're looking at something big here," said Steve Ruzika, president of ADT's electronic security services division.
Ruzika discussed the CARCOP system at a two-day conference about mergers and acquisitions in the security industry. It was sponsored by several organizations, including Lehman Brothers.
ADT will launch CARCOP in Miami and Atlanta on October 1, with a national roll-out set for next year. It will cost $500 to $900 with additional monthly monitoring fees of less than $20.
Ruzika expressed confidence about the expected sales for the new system, saying that internal projections of 100,000 units to be installed next year are "reasonably conservative."

Once a CARCOP unit is installed, the ADT monitoring center can track a vehicle's movements, remotely unlock doors, roll down windows or disable the car. Motorists can also use a personal code to trigger an alarm system once they are inside the vehicle. ADT's control center will be notified if the vehicle's door is opened while the system is engaged.

Ruzika declined to disclose the company's financial projections for CARCOP, but indicated labor costs for the new system will not be significant because vehicles installed with the CARCOP system will be monitored at ADT's existing control centers. Distributors will install the units.
"This company has the resources and the distribution channel and the relationships to make a dent in this market," said Andrew Jeffrey, an analyst at Robertson Stephens & Co.
ADT previously has discussed the CARCOP system with industry analysts, but the company apparently has not promoted it heavily outside Wall Street.
Ruzika said ADT is working with insurance companies so that motorists who buy the CARCOP system will receive a discount on their premiums.
He said ADT faces little competition on the CARCOP system. Several other companies provide a similar service, "but in a smaller way", he said.
